name: Bar / brewery / taproom
summary: Production brewery with on-site taproom (≈3,000–15,000 SF; roughly 35–45% taproom/front-of-house, the rest brewhouse, cellar, cold storage and packaging) plus patio. Construction blends a bar-restaurant front of house with a wet light-industrial production floor (trench drains, sloped slabs, glycol and process utilities); the brewhouse and cellar tanks are equipment line items. No authoritative cost source for this type was found (search quota ran out), so the baseline is derived from the full-service restaurant data in this folder, RSMeans 2019 factory and social-club models, and bar-centric franchise disclosures, with low-confidence industry guides for equipment.

typicalSize.method: Industry guide space need 3,000–8,000 SF (b5); a 7-bbl ground-up brewery/taproom built at 5,457 SF (b7). High end for regional production with packaging hall. Mid 7,000 SF.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre assuming ~0.25–0.3 FAR typical of freestanding restaurant/light-industrial pads with patio and parking (compare restaurant-full-service ≈3,900 SF/ac; production space needs less parking). Judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Taproom/assembly area parked like a bar (≈1 per 50–100 SF of FOH) and production like industrial (≈1 per 1,000 SF); with FOH ≈40% → 0.006–0.015 per gross SF. Judgment; local codes vary widely.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Blend by program: taproom/FOH (40%) at ~$400/SF = full-service restaurant mid $475 (restaurant-full-service.json, from Applebee's/Chili's FDDs) less ~15% for a lighter kitchen; production/cellar (60%) at ~$260/SF = RSMeans 2019 1-story factory $120/SF building-only (b1) scaled by the same field-to-RSMeans ratio observed for restaurants (franchise $475 incl. site vs RSMeans $205 → ~2.3× incl. escalation and site; applied at ~2.15× for simpler industrial site) — plus wet-process premium. 0.4×400 + 0.6×260 = $316 → mid $315. Cross-checks: RSMeans 2019 social club $157/SF building-only (b2); bar-centric restaurant new construction Twin Peaks $2.9–5.0M for 6,000–8,000 SF ≈ $360–830/SF incl. deposits (b3) is the ceiling for an all-FOH program; a 7-bbl brewery/taproom ground-up at 5,457 SF is reported at $1.1M (b7, year not stated, so not used numerically). Low $210 = PEMB production-heavy; high $475 = taproom-heavy, restaurant-grade finishes.

scope.notes: Ground-up building incl. taproom bar build-out, restrooms, small kitchen, production floor with trench drains and sloped slab, process water/gas/power rough-ins, walk-in cold-room shell, and typical on-site work. Excludes brewhouse, cellar tanks, glycol, packaging equipment, draft system (line items/FF&E), land, soft costs, impact/tap and sewer-capacity fees. Conversions of existing industrial shells typically run well below the baseline.

qualityTiers.method: low/mid (210/315) and high/mid (475/315 ≈ 1.5); luxury for destination brewpubs with full restaurants and event space. Judgment.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the restaurant-full-service split with production adjustments: heavier 03 (thick sloped slabs), 22 (trench drains, process water, floor drains), 26 (brewhouse power), 13 (insulated cold-room panels); lighter 09 finishes in production. Site 0.19 incl. patio.

lineItems.name: Brewhouse system (mash/lauter tun, kettle/whirlpool, HLT) 5–15 bbl, installed

cost.method: Guides: 5–10 bbl brewhouse $100,000–$150,000, 'sometimes up to $350,000' (b5); brewhouse system 'between $50,000 and $500,000 or more' (b6). Mid $250k assumes a 10–15 bbl steam/direct-fire system with installation and process piping. Low-confidence sources.

lineItems.notes: Scales with barrel size, not SF.

lineItems.name: Fermenters, brite tanks and glycol chiller

cost.method: Fermenters 5–10 bbl $3,500–$10,000 each and glycol $5,000–$15,000 (b5); brite tanks $5,000–$40,000 and glycol $10,000–$50,000 (b6). Mid ≈ 6 FVs + 2 brites (20 bbl) + glycol ≈ $120k.

lineItems.notes: Add packaging (canning line, keg washer $10–14k per b5) separately if needed.

lineItems.name: Process wastewater pretreatment (solids interceptor, pH neutralization, sampling port)

cost.method: Judgment: many sewer utilities require brewery pretreatment; cost from comparable grease-interceptor + neutralization tank installations. Verify with local pretreatment ordinance.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out inside Div 22; sewer capacity/strength surcharges excluded (fees).

lineItems.name: Patio / beer garden (paving, fencing, shade, lighting)

cost.method: Judgment, aligned with restaurant-full-service outdoor-patio item (lower finish level).

lineItems.notes: Catalog description includes a patio; switch on when programmed.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Taproom interiors/furniture $50,000–$150,000, draft system/glassware/POS $10,000–$25,000, basic kitchen $20,000–$40,000 (b5) → $80–215k on 3,000–8,000 SF ≈ $15–45/SF; high allows full-service kitchen.

pctOfHard.method: A&E incl. process engineering (≈7–9%), permits, legal and licensing. Licensing (brewing, sales, environmental) ≈ $5,000–$20,000 and legal $2,000–$20,000 (b5). Judgment for the percentage.

softCosts.notes: Type-specific: federal TTB brewer's notice and state manufacturer/on-premise licenses; sewer pretreatment permits. Liquor-license cost varies by state (see restaurant-full-service notes).

design.method: Process layout often finalized after equipment purchase; judgment.

hard.method: Judgment; a 2026 news report notes a taproom project's construction costs 'had increased by 30%' after design completion (b8), indicating high volatility.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $210–475 × 1.10–1.18; min allows shell conversions, max a restaurant-heavy brewpub (b3 ceiling). Excludes equipment and land.

source.title: Natural State Beer Company — project page

evidence.scopeNotes: Sizing/program only. Page also states a cost of $1,100,000 for 5,457 SF (~$202/SF) with a seven-barrel, two-vessel brewhouse, but no project year, so it is not used as a dated cost point.

source.title: Olde Mecklenburg Brewery's Mount Holly taproom on track to open despite cost increase

evidence.scopeNotes: January 5, 2026 article; no dollar amounts. Used only to support a higher hard-cost contingency.

openQuestions: No sourced, dated ground-up brewery/taproom construction cost — web search quota ran out. Look for Brewers Association startup surveys, state/municipal brewery incentive agreements, or SBA-financed project budgets.
Baseline is a program-weighted blend of restaurant and industrial proxies; verify the 40/60 FOH/production split for the project.
Equipment line items rely on vendor blogs.
